metadata.title: Kaseya Unitrends Backup Attack Graph
metadata.analysis_summary: All 8 attack paths identified with 100% consistency across 5 independent analyses and verified against source data. Attack graph reveals multiple exploitation chains including incomplete fix relationships, similar attack patterns, and precondition-based escalation paths.

nodes.description: bpserverd proprietary protocol authentication bypass leading to remote code execution with root privileges
nodes.vulnerability_type: Authentication Bypass leading to Remote Code Execution
nodes.precondition: network access to bpserverd service through xinetd
nodes.postcondition: arbitrary command execution with root privileges

nodes.description: api/storage web interface input validation bypass leading to authentication bypass and RCE
nodes.vulnerability_type: Input Validation Bypass leading to Authentication Bypass and RCE
nodes.precondition: network access to api/storage web interface
nodes.postcondition: authentication bypassed and arbitrary commands executed with root privileges

nodes.description: User interface authentication bypass allowing command injection via /api/hosts using backquotes
nodes.vulnerability_type: Authentication Bypass leading to Command Injection
nodes.precondition: network access to user interface /api/hosts endpoint
nodes.postcondition: authentication bypassed and arbitrary command injection via backquotes

nodes.description: Privilege escalation from read-only user to admin
bpserverd daemon remote code execution via untrusted input passed to system calls as root
nodes.vulnerability_type: Remote Code Execution via Command Injection
nodes.precondition: ability to send untrusted input to bpserverd daemon

nodes.description: World writable file allowing local privilege escalation to apache user
nodes.vulnerability_type: Local Privilege Escalation via Insecure File Permissions

nodes.description: Weak password for PostgreSQL wguest account
nodes.precondition: knowledge of weak password or brute force capability

nodes.description: wguest account privilege escalation to postgres via PostgreSQL trigger function injection
nodes.vulnerability_type: Privilege Escalation via SQL Trigger Injection
nodes.postcondition: postgres user privileges obtained via trigger function injection

nodes.description: vaultServer format string vulnerability via crafted HTTP request
nodes.precondition: ability to send crafted HTTP requests to vaultServer
nodes.postcondition: potential code execution in privileged vaultServer context

nodes.description: apache user arbitrary file read capability via insecure Sudo rule abuse
nodes.vulnerability_type: Arbitrary File Read via Sudo Misconfiguration
nodes.postcondition: ability to read sensitive files including /etc/shadow

links.description: Both vulnerabilities exploit authentication bypass mechanisms in Unitrends Backup versions before 10.0.0 to achieve arbitrary command execution with root privileges through different attack surfaces (bpserverd vs api/storage web interface). They share the same fundamental attack principle of bypassing authentication controls to gain root-level remote code execution.
links.evidence: CVE-2017-12477 targets bpserverd daemon authentication bypass; CVE-2017-12478 targets api/storage input validation bypass. Both achieve identical postcondition: arbitrary command execution with root privileges in same affected version range (< 10.0.0).

links.description: CVE-2018-6328 affects versions before 10.1.0, demonstrating that authentication bypass vulnerabilities persisted after the 10.0.0 patch that was intended to resolve CVE-2017-12477. This represents an incomplete fix where the root cause of authentication bypass was not fully addressed in the initial patch.
links.evidence: CVE-2017-12477 patched in version 10.0.0; CVE-2018-6328 still exists in versions < 10.1.0, indicating authentication bypass vulnerabilities continued to exist post-patch.

links.description: CVE-2018-6328 affects versions before 10.1.0, demonstrating that authentication bypass vulnerabilities persisted after the 10.0.0 patch that was intended to resolve CVE-2017-12478. This represents an incomplete fix where the fundamental authentication bypass weakness was not comprehensively addressed.
links.evidence: CVE-2017-12478 patched in version 10.0.0; CVE-2018-6328 still exists in versions < 10.1.0, indicating authentication bypass vulnerabilities continued to exist post-patch.

links.description: Both vulnerabilities target the bpserverd daemon component and achieve arbitrary command execution as root through command injection mechanisms. Despite being discovered years apart, they exploit the same fundamental weakness: untrusted input being passed to system calls in the bpserverd daemon, resulting in root-level remote code execution.
links.evidence: CVE-2017-12477: bpserverd authentication bypass leading to arbitrary commands with root privilege; CVE-2021-43033: bpserverd daemon vulnerable to RCE as root via untrusted input passed to system calls. Both target same component with same attack principle.

links.description: CVE-2021-40385 enables privilege escalation from read-only user to admin, and the resulting admin privileges satisfy the user authentication precondition required to exploit CVE-2021-40387's authenticated remote code execution vulnerability. This creates a direct exploitation chain where initial low-privilege access can be escalated to achieve code execution.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-40385 postcondition: Admin privileges obtained; CVE-2021-40387 precondition: User authentication required. Admin privileges satisfy authentication requirement.

links.description: CVE-2021-43034 allows local users to achieve code execution as the apache user through exploitation of world-writable file permissions. This apache user access is the exact precondition required to exploit CVE-2021-43043, which allows the apache user to read arbitrary files including /etc/shadow through sudo misconfiguration abuse.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-43034 postcondition: code execution as apache user; CVE-2021-43043 precondition: apache user access required. Direct precondition match.

links.description: CVE-2021-43036 provides access to the PostgreSQL wguest account through a weak default password. This wguest account access is the exact precondition required to exploit CVE-2021-43038, which allows privilege escalation from wguest to postgres user via PostgreSQL trigger function injection. This creates a clear privilege escalation path within the database system.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-43036 postcondition: wguest PostgreSQL account access; CVE-2021-43038 precondition: wguest PostgreSQL account access. Exact precondition match.

links.description: Both vulnerabilities exploit memory corruption weaknesses in the privileged vaultServer component. CVE-2021-43041 uses a format string vulnerability triggered by crafted HTTP requests, while CVE-2021-43042 uses a buffer overflow. Despite different exploitation techniques, they share the same fundamental attack principle: memory corruption in the privileged vaultServer to achieve code execution.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-43041: format string vulnerability in privileged vaultServer; CVE-2021-43042: buffer overflow in vaultServer component. Both target same component through memory corruption mechanisms.
